claims.statement: GHEC-only guide permissions metadata requires repository admin to change Pages visibility. Private-site capability requires organization GHEC; trial link is product information, not permission for signup or cost.

Privately published project sites restrict access to repository readers. Managed-user enterprise sites are private-only and accessible only to enterprise members; retain both repository-read and enterprise-identity conditions rather than infer every enterprise member reads every private site.

Non-managed GHEC organizations may choose public internet or private project publication. Access control applies to organization-owned private/internal repository project sites, not organization sites; private repository alone does not prove private website.

Private sites use distinct unique subdomains from public sites, described as TLS-certified under pages.github.io with HSTS and separate origins against cross-repository cookie tossing. These are source platform claims, not measured TLS/header/session behavior for a target or custom-domain certificate guarantee.

Pages settings exposes unique subdomain; static generators configured around repository-name path may need adaptation after private transition. Endpoint/path change is separate from access control and requires URL/build/asset verification.
Custom domains can shorten privately published site names but require separately reviewed domain configuration and verification; no domain, DNS or site visibility changed.

UI procedure navigates site repository/settings/Pages, selects visibility and Visit site. Menu selection and a displayed URL do not prove effective public denial or authorized-reader access; admin authorization remains separate.

Reusable filename twenty-minutes-to-publish actually describes up to ten minutes after push, with troubleshooting after an hour. Preserve content over filename and distinguish publication propagation from deployment timeout; no timed native observation performed.

Trial, custom-domain, limits, origin-security and generator references remain separately scoped. No site publication, credentials, costs, rights clearance, accepted control or native enforcement receipt follows; source/published completeness requires independent assurance.
